speech: Wanna fight?
Ah, you come for fight, ja?
You look funny.
Grrr!
What you want?
Go Away!
Hello.
What are you doing in our village, outlander?
Nothing much.
Bah! Go down to the longhall, and there you will find excitement aplenty! Our finest warrior, Gunthor the Brave, will give you a rousing welcome!
I'll bear it in mind.
I'm exploring.
Bah! You cannot hope to learn anything of us just by strolling through our village! We are an ancient tribe, our ways date back to the time before Avarrocka was founded!
Would you care to tell me more?
Oh? You are not so ignorant as I thought. Very well, I shall speak of our tribe...

Our elders remember that about a century ago we were living in the lands far to the west. We were a large nomadic mountain tribe, settling wherever there was food, moving on when it had run out. As the tribe

grew larger, it was hard to find enough food for everyone, and we were forced to shift our camp more and more often. In time, a warrior called Gunnar took his friends and their families and left the larger tribe,
moving south in search of new places. They eventually settled here and built this village, finding that the old nomadic traditions were no longer needed.
Our current chieftain, Gunthor the Brave, is a direct- line descendent of Gunnar.

However, our ways have changed little in the last century. Although more and more people use magical powers, we do not believe it is wise to take upon oneself the power of the gods in this way. To this day, we fight

with the mighty sword, the vicious axe and the swift arrow on the wind. Some of our young, wishing to try so-called 'civilisation' and the softness of city life, abandon the tribe and move to the cities. It is sad to
see them go, but we do not prevent them; we live here in our village because we love this life - we do not force it on those whom it does not suit.
There, I have said enough.
Thank you.
You look like a load of primitive savages.
And you look like an arrogant fool. And you smell like a raccoon's bottom.
I'm bored.
I came to kill you all!
Ho ho! Brave words indeed from an outerlander! Go down to the longhall and try it!
Hello there.
Ha Ha! Hello!
Who are you?
I'm Sigurd the Great and Brainy.
Why do they call you the Great and Brainy?
Because I invented the Log Canoe!
Log Canoe?
Yeash! Me and my cousins were having a great party by the river when we decided to have a game of 'Smack The Tree'
Smack the Tree?
It's a game were you take it in turnsh shmacking a tree. First one to uproot the tree winsh!
Anyway, I won the game with a flying tackle. The tree came loose and down the river bank I went, still holding the tree.
I woke up a few hours later and found myself several miles down river. And thatsh how I invented the log canoe!
So you invented the 'Log Canoe' by falling into a river hugging a tree?
Well I refined the design from the original you know!
I cut all the branches off to make it more comfortable. I could tell you how to if you like?
No thanks, not right now.
Can you teach me about canoes?
Well, you don't look like you have the skill to make a canoe.
You need to have at least level 12 woodcutting.
Once you are able to make a canoe it makes travel along the river much quicker!
It's really quite simple. Just walk down to that tree on the bank and chop it down.
Then take your axe to it and shape it how you like!
You can make a log canoe like mine! It'll get you 1 stop down the river.
There's some snooty fella down near the Champions Guild who reckons his canoes are better than mine. He's never said it to my face though.
You could make a Dugout canoe with your woodcutting skill, but I don't see why you would want to.
Well, you're pretty handy with an axe!
You could make Stable Dugout canoes, like that snooty fella Tarquin.
He reckons his canoes are better than mine. He's never said it to my face though.
You look like you know your way around a tree, you can make a Waka canoe.
What's a Waka?
I've only ever seen Hari using them. People say he's found a way to canoe the river underground and into the Wilderness
Hari hangs around up near Edgeville
He's a nice bloke.
Oooh, my dear, have you heard the news?
Okay, tell me about the news.
It's terrible, absolutely terrible! Those poor people!
Okay, yeah.
And who'd have ever thought such a sweet old gentleman would do such a thing?
I really don't know what you're talking about.
Oooh, my dear, had you not heard?
At this rate I don't think I want to know...
Oh, you must quickly go and speak to the bank guard outside the bank. He'll tell you all about it, oooh, such a shock it was...

I, my dear, am a concerned citizen of Draynor Village. Ever since the Council allowed those farmers to set up their stalls here, we've had a constant flow of thieves and murderers through our fair village, and I decided
that someone HAD to stand up and keep an eye on the situation.
I also do voluntary work for the Draynor Manor Restoration Fund. We're campaigning to have Draynor Manor turned into a museum before the wet-rot destroys it completely.
Right...
I'm not talking to you, you horrible woman.
Oooh.
Hi, who are you guarding here?
Can't say, all very secret. You should get out of here. I am not supposed to talk while I guard.
Hey, chill out, I won't cause you trouble. I was just wondering what you do to relax.
You never relax with these people, but it's a good career for a young man.
I had better leave, I don't want trouble.
Thanks, I appreciate that. Talking on duty can be punishable by having your mouth stitched up. These are tough people, no mistake.
